intent: The supporting sentence under a PopoverTitle that describes the popover's panel to assistive technology.
typical_uses: A sentence stating what the popover's controls change

dont_use_when.situation: The supporting text under a dialog's title
The supporting text under a card's title on the page

invariants.text: PopoverDescription renders a p in the muted foreground color; popover.module.css sets no margin on it, so the browser's own paragraph margins still apply.

anti_patterns.dont: Put the popover's form fields or long content inside PopoverDescription
anti_patterns.do_instead: Keep it to a short sentence and place fields and long content in PopoverContent after the header

render.states: render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies
render.because: Base UI's render prop takes an element or a function of the description's state, so its type is a union of a React element and a callback - the compiler emits one JSON type per property; the primitive passes an empty state object.

style.states: style accepts a function as well as a plain style object; the primitive passes that function an empty state object
style.because: Base UI widens React's `CSSProperties` to `CSSProperties | ((state) => CSSProperties)`, and the description's state carries no fields. The compiler emits one JSON type per property, so nothing is asserted; the kit's own styling goes through popover.module.css, not through this.

bad.title: A form inside the description
bad.why: Everything inside the description becomes the popup's accessible description through `aria-describedby`, field included.

render.description: TS: ReactElement<unknown, string | JSXElementConstructor<any>> | ComponentRenderFn<HTMLProps, PopoverDescriptionState> | undefined. The compiler emits one JSON type per property; this type is left to tsc. render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies.
